_about: Simplified, illustrative model for education, not a microclimate simulation (see ENVI-met or PALM-4U for that). Edit any value and reload.

shade._about: Felt temperature drop inside a crown shadow. Scaled by sun altitude; full effect from full_effect_sun_altitude_deg.

evapotranspiration._about: Air cooling around each tree (Gaussian, sigma_m), saturating at max_total_C for many trees; scaled by night_factor after sunset.

pollution._about: Particulate matter (PM10, PM2.5): % change of the street's concentration with full crown cover, scaled linearly by the crown cover of the street corridor.
pollution._canyon_increase_pct: Street canyon: trees raise concentrations. Lower end of the +26 to +96 % reported by Abhijith et al. (2017).
pollution._deposition_pct_full_cover: Open street: deposition on leaves. Nowak et al. (2006): about 0.7 % PM10 improvement at 33 % city tree cover.
pollution._canyon_max_halfwidth_m: Buildings within this distance of the street axis on both sides make a point of the section count as street canyon.

noise._about: Road traffic noise: change in dB from new street trees.
noise._tree_row_dB: Rows of street trees are not tree belts; measured reductions need dense belts of 15-20 m depth (Van Renterghem et al. 2015).

grid._about: Inverse distance weighting of the overlay points. Above dense_point_threshold points, only points within idw_radius_m count.

street_view._about: Before/after panel of the street view (street.js). Temperature: the tree model above on a hot afternoon (air_temperature_C), plus the waste heat of the vehicles placed, as for the map's traffic measure (measures.traffic.C_per_W_m2). Pollution: the urban background plus the traffic placed, scaled from the measured traffic share at Heilbronn's traffic station by each vehicle type's emission factor; trees then change the street's concentration as in 'pollution' (street canyon: higher). Each vehicle placed stands for trips_per_day of its type. Estimates with typical values, not measurements.
street_view._no2_background_ugm3: Urban background station DEBW015 Heilbronn, NO2 annual means 2022-2025: 19, 17, 16, 18 µg/m³ (UBA air data).
street_view._pm25_background_ugm3: Urban background PM2.5 in Heilbronn, rounded; the traffic station adds 0.4-0.7 µg/m³ (measures.traffic._pm).
street_view._reference: What the traffic adds at the traffic station DEBW152 Weinsberger Straße-Ost (a primary road, about 15,000 vehicles a day assumed, as in measures.traffic): NO2 traffic minus background 13, 12, 14, 9 µg/m³ in 2022-2025 (UBA), PM2.5 0.4-0.7 µg/m³. The emission factors are those of its fleet: mostly cars, a few per cent buses and lorries.
street_view._trips_per_day: Each vehicle placed stands for this many trips a day of its type along the street, about one every 5 minutes in the daytime, like a frequent bus line.
street_view._canyon: Weipertstraße has buildings close on both sides, so trees count as in a street canyon (pollution.canyon_increase_pct).
street_view._vehicles: Typical urban values for the German fleet, rounded, order of magnitude as in HBEFA 4.2 / UBA TREMOD: NOx per km (car: mix of petrol and diesel, Euro 4-6; bus: 12 m Euro VI diesel city bus, real-world urban 0.3-1.5 g/km), PM2.5 per km including brake, tyre and road wear, energy per km = fuel (car 6 l/100 km, bus 40 l/100 km, motorbike 4 l/100 km); a bicycle's is the rider's body heat. People per vehicle: car 1.4 (MiD 2017), bus 20 (average load of a German city bus), motorbike 1.1.
street_view._area_lateral_m: The street between its building fronts, metres from the centre line (east +): OpenStreetMap buildings at 13.5-14.6 m west (way 35710237) and 9.5-10.7 m east (ways 84722898, 84722906, 84722908, 84722910, 84722915) within 60 m of the camera point. Means and the shaded area are over this area in both directions.

placement._about: Where trees may go. Road half widths (m) by OSM class; footways and pedestrian zones are not obstacles.
placement._crown_overlap: New trees may overlap each other's crowns down to this fraction of the summed radii.
placement._existing_tree_spacing: Distance to an existing tree as a fraction of both crown radii; 1 = crowns may not overlap.
placement._existing_trees_claim_side: Evenly spaced trees: an existing tree within half a spacing claims its side of the street, so the new tree goes to the other side (or is skipped if both sides have trees).

measures._about: Measures selectable in the scenario panel, one at a time, listed in 'order' (by how well they fit a street in Heilbronn). 'note' is shown under the selector.

trees.label: Street trees
trees.note: Strongest and best-studied cooling: shade plus evaporation. Needs room for roots and a decade to grow.

sails.label: Shade sails
sails.note: Fabric stretched over the pavement or across the street. Shade from day one where trees cannot grow; needs anchors on facades or masts and comes down in winter.
sails._sails: Number of sails: default, max. Over the pavements they alternate sides like trees; across the street they span it.
sails._shade_factor: Share of the full tree-shade cooling (shade.max_cooling_C) under a sail: fabric lets some sun through and warms up.
sails._across: Across the street: width = road plus pavement_m on both sides, high enough for lorries (4.5 m clearance).

beds.label: Grass & flower beds
beds.note: Unseal a strip along the kerb (parking or wide pavement). Cools the ground a lot and the air a little; no shade.
beds._width: Bed width in metres: default, min, max. Beds go on both sides, behind the kerb, where there is no building or other road.
beds._air: Air cooling from each m² of bed: Gaussian (sigma_m), saturating at max_total_C; × night_factor after sunset.
beds._felt_on_bed_C: Felt temperature drop standing on the bed in full sun (cooler ground radiates less), scaled like shade.

pavement.label: Reflective road surface
pavement.note: A light coating on the roadway. Cools the road surface, barely the air, and reflects sun onto people walking by.
pavement._albedo: Albedo after coating: default, min, max.
pavement._air: Air cooling per +0.1 albedo over the road, in full sun; × night_factor after sunset. Fades to 0 over fade_m beside the road.
pavement._reflected: Felt temperature rise per +0.1 albedo from reflected sun, on the road and sidewalk_m beside it, scaled like shade.

misting.label: Misting poles
misting.note: Fine water spray, as on Spanish terraces. Strong but very local, needs water and hygiene checks, weaker in humid weather.
misting._poles: Number of poles: default, max. Placed evenly on alternating sides like trees.

traffic.label: Speed limit & less traffic
traffic.note: Tempo 30 or fewer cars mostly cut noise. Engine heat is small, so the cooling is close to zero; fewer cars lower particles a little.
traffic._current_limit_kmh: Assumed current limit by road class.
traffic._vehicles_per_day: Assumed motor vehicles per day by road class (no counts per street).
traffic._heat: Waste heat per vehicle and km (a car using 6 l/100 km), spread over the roadway around the clock.
traffic._fuel_factor_30: Fuel use at 30 instead of 50 km/h; studies find anything from a little less to a little more, depending on traffic flow.
traffic._pm: Particulate matter: share of a street's PM that its own traffic adds, from the Heilbronn station pair (traffic DEBW152 Weinsberger Straße-Ost, a primary road, minus urban background DEBW015), annual means 2022-2025 (UBA). Conservative approximation, see README 'Traffic and particulate matter'.
traffic._pm_reference_vehicles_per_day: Vehicles per day assumed at the reference station (road class primary). Quieter roads scale down linearly; busier ones are capped at the measured share.
traffic._pm_factor_30: Traffic PM at 30 instead of 50 km/h. Studies disagree (exhaust not lower in Stuttgart, about -2 ± 3 % elsewhere), so no change.

sources._about: Shown under 'Model sources' in the scenario panel. {a.b} is replaced by that parameter's value. 'measure' shows a part only for that measure.
sources.note: The parameters are rough estimates, checked against these studies, not fitted to measurements.

parts.model: up to −{shade.max_cooling_C} °C in full shade, full effect from a sun height of {shade.full_effect_sun_altitude_deg}°
parts.observed: Tree shade lowers the felt temperature (PET) by 7–15 °C on hot days.

refs.title: Rahman & Ennos (2016): What we know and don't know about the cooling benefits of urban trees. Trees & Design Action Group

parts.model: −{evapotranspiration.per_tree_C} °C per tree, at most −{evapotranspiration.max_total_C} °C, fading over about {evapotranspiration.sigma_m} m, × {evapotranspiration.night_factor} at night
parts.observed: Air under a canopy measured 0.5–1.8 °C cooler than outside in Munich; other cities 0.1–2.8 °C. At night, green areas can cool more than by day.

refs.title: Rahman, Moser, Gold, Rötzer & Pauleit (2018): Vertical air temperature gradients under the shade of two contrasting urban tree species during different types of summer days. Science of the Total Environment 633, 100–111
Rahman & Ennos (2016): What we know and don't know about the cooling benefits of urban trees. Trees & Design Action Group

parts.model: {measures.sails.shade_factor} × the tree shade: up to −{shade.max_cooling_C} °C felt in full shade, shadow projected from the sail height along the sun ray; no air cooling
parts.observed: In Tempe, Arizona, people in shade felt about one point cooler on a 9-point scale, and a shade canopy worked as well as tree shade. Tree shade lowers the felt temperature (PET) by 7–15 °C on hot days.

refs.title: Middel, Selover, Hagen & Chhetri (2016): Impact of shade on outdoor thermal comfort—a seasonal field study in Tempe, Arizona. International Journal of Biometeorology 60, 1849–1861
Rahman & Ennos (2016): What we know and don't know about the cooling benefits of urban trees. Trees & Design Action Group

parts.model: −{measures.beds.per_m2_C} °C per m² of bed nearby, at most −{measures.beds.max_total_C} °C air cooling; −{measures.beds.felt_on_bed_C} °C felt on the bed in full sun
parts.observed: In Manchester, grass lowered the ground temperature by up to 24 °C but hardly changed globe (felt) or air temperature; tree shade lowered globe temperature by 5–7 °C.

refs.title: Armson, Stringer & Ennos (2012): The effect of tree shade and grass on surface and globe temperatures in an urban area. Urban Forestry & Urban Greening 11, 245–255

parts.model: −{measures.pavement.air_C_per_0_1_albedo} °C air per +0.1 albedo in full sun (× {measures.pavement.night_factor} at night), +{measures.pavement.reflected_felt_C_per_0_1_albedo} °C felt per +0.1 albedo on road and pavement
parts.observed: Coated streets in Los Angeles were 4–6 °C cooler at the surface, the air only 0.5 °C cooler in the afternoon and about 0.1 °C at night, while the radiant heat on pedestrians was 4 °C higher at midday.

refs.title: Middel, Turner, Schneider, Hu & Stiller (2020): Solar reflective pavements—A policy panacea to heat mitigation? Environmental Research Letters 15, 064016

parts.model: −{measures.misting.per_pole_C} °C per pole, at most −{measures.misting.max_total_C} °C, fading over about {measures.misting.sigma_m} m, switched on {measures.misting.operating_hours.0}–{measures.misting.operating_hours.1} h
parts.observed: Field studies measured roughly 2–5 °C cooler air near misting systems, more in dry heat and still air, less in humid or windy weather; humidity rises.

refs.title: Ulpiani (2019): Water mist spray for outdoor cooling: A systematic review of technologies, methods and impacts. Applied Energy 254, 113340
Ulpiani, Di Giuseppe, Di Perna, D'Orazio & Zinzi (2019): Thermal comfort improvement in urban spaces with water spray systems: Field measurements and survey. Building and Environment 156, 46–61

parts.model: engine heat {measures.traffic.heat_MJ_per_vehicle_km} MJ per vehicle-km over the roadway, {measures.traffic.C_per_W_m2} °C per W/m²; Tempo 30: fuel × {measures.traffic.fuel_factor_30}, noise {measures.traffic.noise_30_dB} dB(A)
parts.observed: Tempo 30 on main roads lowered noise by 1–4 dB(A) in follow-up measurements. Vehicle heat warms street air mostly at night and by a few tenths of a degree at most.

refs.title: Umweltbundesamt (2016): Lärm- und Klimaschutz durch Tempo 30 (Texte 30/2016, summary)
Spatiotemporal impact of vehicle heat on urban thermal environment: A case study in Hong Kong (PolyU)

parts.model: the street's own traffic adds {measures.traffic.pm_traffic_share.pm10} of PM10 and {measures.traffic.pm_traffic_share.pm25} of PM2.5 on a main road, fewer on quieter roads; that part falls with the traffic; Tempo 30 × {measures.traffic.pm_factor_30}
parts.observed: Heilbronn, annual means 2022–2025: Weinsberger Straße (traffic) 15–17 µg/m³ PM10 against 13–16 at the urban background station, i.e. 1–2 µg/m³ (6–13 %) more; PM2.5 0.4–0.7 µg/m³ (4–8 %) more. In 2016–2018 the difference was still 4–5 µg/m³ PM10. In Berlin around 2000, main streets had up to 40 % more PM10 than the background, half of it from exhaust and tyres, half from stirred-up road dust. Today most traffic PM is not from exhausts but from brakes, tyres and road dust.

refs.title: Umweltbundesamt, air data: annual balances PM10 and PM2.5, stations DEBW152 Heilbronn Weinsberger Straße-Ost and DEBW015 Heilbronn
Lenschow et al. (2001): Some ideas about the sources of PM10. Atmospheric Environment 35, S23–S33

Harrison, Allan, Carruthers, Heal, Lewis, Marner, Murrells & Williams (2021): Non-exhaust vehicle emissions of particulate matter and VOC from road traffic: A review. Atmospheric Environment 262, 118592

parts.model: street canyon: +{pollution.canyon_increase_pct} % with full crown cover; open street: −{pollution.deposition_pct_full_cover} %; scaled by the crown cover of the street (linear scaling is an assumption)
parts.observed: Trees in street canyons raised pollutant concentrations by 26–96 % on average; hedges lowered them by 24–61 % at the footpath; on open roads, dense vegetation barriers lowered them by 15–60 %. City-wide, trees improve PM10 by about 0.7 % (Atlanta, 33 % tree cover).

refs.title: Abhijith, Kumar, Gallagher, McNabola, Baldauf, Pilla, Broderick, Di Sabatino & Pulvirenti (2017): Air pollution abatement performances of green infrastructure in open road and built-up street canyon environments – A review. Atmospheric Environment 162, 71–86
Nowak, Crane & Stevens (2006): Air pollution removal by urban trees and shrubs in the United States. Urban Forestry & Urban Greening 4, 115–123

parts.model: {noise.tree_row_dB} dB for rows of street trees
parts.observed: Measured attenuation by 35 tree belts 20 m deep: below 3, 3–6 or 6–9 dB(A); a 15 m deep optimised belt can match a 1–2 m noise wall. Single rows of trees are not reported to reduce noise.

refs.title: Van Renterghem, Forssén, Attenborough, Jean, Defrance, Hornikx & Kang (2015): Using natural means to reduce surface transport noise during propagation outdoors. Applied Acoustics 92, 86–101

parts.model: computed for the chosen date, time and the city's location

refs.title: SunCalc, a JavaScript library for sun positions (V. Agafonkin)
